name: Dr. Bernd Waschneck
headline: Vice President R&D at Infineon | Chip Design | Semiconductor Manufacturing | Organizational Leadership
summary:
Global semiconductor R&D leader with strong end-to-end perspective from manufacturing/operations to advanced chip development. I scale innovation to commercial success. As Vice President R&D, I lead 330+ engineers across 6 sites in Asia and Europe, driving results in System-on-Chip design, physical implementation, chip‑package‑board co-design (incl. PCB), Design-for-Test, and RTL2GDS methodology. 
    
I build resilient, high-performing organizations, develop leaders, and deliver measurable improvements in execution, productivity, and time-to-market through AI, platform reuse and automation. 
  
I complement deep R&D leadership with hands-on experience in semiconductor operations and manufacturing excellence, including time in the Operations Office supporting the COO - strengthening my ability to align technology roadmaps with business strategy, translate priorities into execution, and drive cross-functional change at scale.
  
Academic background: PhD (AI/ML in Manufacturing Engineering, University of Stuttgart); studies in semiconductor physics and technology management (LMU/CDTM, Munich; NUS, Singapore).
  

 Academic profile: https://scholar.google.de/citations?user=G4oK_VQAAAAJ

positions.title: Interim Head of System Innovation & Software
positions.description:
Leading the global "System Innovation & Software" team within the Power & Sensor Systems division, which comprises of ~110 people at locations in Munich, Dresden, Villach, and Singapore. 

Successfully navigated the team through a period of transformation, driving strategic realignment, restructuring, and site consolidation (including the closure of the Singapore location), with direct accountability to the Division CTO.

positions.title: Senior Director Chip Design
positions.description:
Senior Director, Chip Development within System Innovation for power & sensor systems. Led a ~60 FTE, multi-site organization across Munich, Dresden and Singapore (digital design, analog/layout, application firmware, innovation & demonstrators) with an ~€9M annual budget.

Drove platform-based SoC development, design methodology and agile application firmware development to reduce design cost and accelerate innovation-to-customer—delivering key programs ahead of schedule. Shaped division strategy toward platform-based design and built cross-divisional partnerships to scale platform initiatives.  Delivered critical IP on time, owned end-to-end R&D for an innovation accelerator in wireless power, drove commercialization of AI-enabled edge/control solutions, as well as next-generation sensor ICs. Transformed multiple teams into a unified, skill-based platform organization.
